structure.title: A possibility takes hold
structure.text: The opening follows a prediction into private deliberation and the prospect of acting on it.

structure.title: Keeping power
structure.text: The remaining action examines the work of maintaining authority as fear changes the world Macbeth must govern.

people.name: Banquo
people.text: His fellow soldier and another listener to the witches.

context.title: Prophecy and choice
context.text: Predictions offer information without telling Macbeth what he must do. The distance between hearing a promise and acting on it matters throughout.

passages.quote: All hail, Macbeth! that shalt be king hereafter!

context.title: Kingship and hospitality
context.text: A guest under one's roof is owed protection. A king's visit intensifies that obligation, making domestic space part of political legitimacy.
context.takeaway: A house is never merely a setting.

notice.why: Recurring images make the experience of ambition bodily and intimate.
Possibility can change from an invitation into a threat.

opening: Macbeth is a successful soldier when three strangers tell him he will be king. He could wait to see whether they are right. Instead, he begins imagining what would have to happen to make them right, and his wife recognises an opportunity he is frightened to name. Shakespeare follows an ambition from its first private permission into the practical work of keeping power. The terrible intimacy is that Macbeth can see what he is becoming while he is still choosing it.
